To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
developing B cells undergo dramatic and sequential changes in their responses during development, maturation, and differentiation.
developing B cells undergo dramatic switches in chemokine responses and receptor expression during their maturation and migration from the bone marrow into the periphery.
the developmental stages of B cells are associated with distinct chemokine response profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the development, maturation and migration of B cells from the bone marrow into the periphery.
the mechanisms that govern B cell development in the bone marrow and their migration to and maturation in peripheral lymphoid tissues.
understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms that control lymphocyte development, migration, and activation, and how these processes are altered in disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
B cell development is characterized by a sequential acquisition of responses to different chemokines.
chemokine receptors and their corresponding ligands are not only expressed by B cells but also are involved in B cell development and migration.
chemokine receptor and ligand expression patterns in developing and mature B cells are complex and dynamic and are not simply a function of the developmental stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

B cells undergo dramatic shifts in their chemokine responsiveness during differentiation, and these changes are associated with changes in the expression of chemokines and chemokine receptors, and that these changes are important for the development of the B cell repertoire and the localization of mature B cells in the periphery.
chemokines play a role in all aspects of B cell development and function.
the chemokine response profile of a given cell type is not fixed but rather changes with differentiation, and this may help to define the developmental stage of a given cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemokine responses change dramatically during B cell maturation, and these changes are important in directing B cell maturation in the bone marrow and migration to lymphoid tissues.
chemokine receptor expression and responsiveness to chemokines changes during the course of B cell development and maturation.
B cell subsets have unique chemokine response profiles that are acquired during development and maturation and that are distinct from their homing chemokine receptor expression.
